CHORALE is for collections in which each omics modality was measured on a
different set of individuals. It does not invent sample pairs. It changes the
question to one the observed data can answer.

## What is missing

If one cohort supplies a transcriptome and another a proteome, there is no row
describing the same person twice. An individual-level joint profile is therefore
not merely unknown: it is not observed and cannot be recovered without
additional assumptions or paired bridge data. Methods that require matched
rows, shared features, or a translation learned from paired examples do not
apply directly.

## The common reference frame

CHORALE connects modalities through a vocabulary of named biological concepts.
A concept is a feature set chosen for a stated reason, such as a pathway or a
cell-type signature. Every modality is scored on the same vocabulary before the
phenotype is consulted.

This produces a common table shape: samples by concepts. The measurements that
created the scores may be different, but each column has a declared biological
meaning. Coverage remains explicit because a modality contributes to a concept
only when it measures enough of its members.

## Two questions from one encoding

The common encoding supports two complementary analyses.

**Concept evidence asks a prespecified question.** Within each modality, does a
named concept change with the phenotype after adjustment for shared covariates?
The adjusted effects are combined by inverse-variance weighting. This is a
meta-analysis: each modality estimates an effect that it could have estimated
alone, and integration improves the evidence when modalities agree.

**Joint-state analysis asks a multivariate question.** Do several concepts vary
together across the stacked collection? CHORALE standardises concept scores
within modality, optionally removes modality-local nuisance effects, and fits a
low-rank representation over the observed entries. The resulting components
are directions through concept space shared by construction. They are fitted
summaries, not uniquely identified mechanisms.

## Three safeguards against easy stories

Concept families test whether overlapping concepts move together without
pretending they are independent. Leave-one-modality-out transfer asks whether a
joint direction estimated from the other modalities predicts phenotype in a
cohort that contributed none of its samples or assay structure. Free dimensions
retain coordinated variation that the vocabulary cannot name.

These answer different questions. A concept can be supported without belonging
to a strong joint component; a joint component can be significant without every
modality carrying it equally; and a free dimension can be real while remaining
biologically unnamed.

## What significance means

The design is held fixed during calibration. CHORALE fits the reduced model
without the effect under test, exchanges its residuals, and rebuilds the score.
This Freedman--Lane procedure preserves the observed relation between phenotype
and adjusting covariates. Family-wise p-values protect against any false call in
the tested family, while q-values estimate the false-discovery proportion among
calls. Neither is a causal claim.

## What a result can establish

A supported concept is an adjusted phenotype association in a named piece of
biology, measured in the modalities listed in its row, at a stated error rate.
A transferred joint component is a multiconcept direction fitted without the
held-out modality that still predicts its phenotype. Neither result reconstructs
an individual's missing modalities or orders cause and consequence.

An absence of significant rows also has several meanings. The analysis may not
have been supplied, the quantity may not have been estimable, or it may have
been tested and failed to beat its null. CHORALE reports these states separately
because only the last is a statistical negative result.
